subproblem.title: Negating the first vector of an orthonormal frame keeps it orthonormal with the same span and negates every covector value
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P), indexed by Fin (d + 1). Then there is an orthonormal family w = (w_0, …, w_d) in ℝ^P with span{w_0, …, w_d} = span{v_0, …, v_d} and β(w_0, …, w_d) = −β(v_0, …, v_d) for every (d+1)-covector β on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ v → ∃ w : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ w ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) ∧ ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), β w = -β v
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the selected proof ("If s = −1, let v' := (−v_0, v_1, …, v_d) (Function.update v 0 (−v_0)): v' is orthonormal, span{v'} = span{v} = V, and β(v') = −β(v) by linearity of β in its first argument (MultilinearMap.map_update_smul / map_neg on β.toAlternatingMap)").
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; Function.update f i x is f with its i-th entry replaced by x; a (d+1)-covector is β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1) = Euclid P [⋀^Fin (d + 1)]→L[ℝ] ℝ; 0 is the first index of Fin (d + 1), which exists because d + 1 ≥ 1.
1. (Signs.) Let c : Fin (d+1) → ℝ, c := Function.update (fun _ => 1) 0 (−1), i.e. c_0 = −1 and c_i = 1 for i ≠ 0; then c_i·c_i = 1 for every i. Let w := Function.update v 0 (−v_0) = (−v_0, v_1, …, v_d). Then w_i = c_i • v_i for every i: for i = 0 both sides equal −v_0, and for i ≠ 0 both sides equal v_i.
2. (w is orthonormal.) For all i, j: ⟨w_i, w_j⟩ = ⟨c_i • v_i, c_j • v_j⟩ = c_i·(c_j·⟨v_i, v_j⟩) (real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right), and ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = [i = j] because v is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite). If i = j this equals c_i·(c_i·1) = 1 by step 1; if i ≠ j it equals c_i·(c_j·0) = 0. Thus ⟨w_i, w_j⟩ = [i = j] for all i, j, i.e. w is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite).
3. (Equal spans.) Each w_i = c_i • v_i is a scalar multiple of an element of range v, hence lies in span(range v); so span(range w) ≤ span(range v) (Submodule.span_le, Submodule.smul_mem, Submodule.subset_span). Conversely, by step 1, v_i = (c_i·c_i) • v_i = c_i • (c_i • v_i) = c_i • w_i (one_smul, smul_smul) lies in span(range w); so span(range v) ≤ span(range w). By antisymmetry span{w_0, …, w_d} = span{v_0, …, v_d}.
4. (Covector values change sign.) Let β be a (d+1)-covector. Linearity of β in its 0-th argument gives β(update v 0 ((−1) • v_0)) = (−1) • β(update v 0 v_0) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_update_smul), and update v 0 v_0 = v (Function.update_eq_self). Since (−1) • x = −x (neg_one_smul), the left side is β(w) and the right side is −β(v); hence β(w) = −β(v).
5. (Conclusion.) w is orthonormal, span{w_0, …, w_d} = span{v_0, …, v_d}, and β(w) = −β(v) for every (d+1)-covector β. ∎

theorem Submission.cbr_ci_cp_exists_orthonormal_frame_eval_neg : ∀ (P d : ℕ) (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ v → ∃ w : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ w ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) ∧ ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), β w = -β v := by
  intro P d v hv
  let c : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ := Function.update (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) 0 (-1)
  have hc : ∀ i, c i * c i = 1 := by
    intro i
    by_cases h : i = 0
    · subst h; simp [c]
    · simp [c, h]
  have hw : (fun i => c i • v i) = Function.update v 0 (-v 0) := by
    funext i
    by_cases h : i = 0
    · subst h; simp [c]
    · simp [c, h]
  refine ⟨Function.update v 0 (-v 0), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [← hw]
    rw [orthonormal_iff_ite] at hv ⊢
    intro i j
    rw [real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right, hv i j]
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst hij
      simp only [↓reduceIte, mul_one]
      exact hc i
    · simp only [hij, ↓reduceIte, mul_zero]
  · rw [← hw]
    apply le_antisymm
    · rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
      exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩)
    · rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
      have h : v i = c i • (c i • v i) := by
        rw [smul_smul, hc i, one_smul]
      rw [h]
      exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩)
  · intro β
    have h := β.map_update_smul v 0 (-1 : ℝ) (v 0)
    rw [neg_one_smul, Function.update_eq_self] at h
    rw [h, neg_one_smul]
proof_key_steps: Take c := update 1 0 (−1) (so c_i·c_i = 1) and w := update v 0 (−v_0), so that w_i = c_i • v_i.
⟨w_i, w_j⟩ = c_i c_j ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = [i = j], so w is orthonormal.
w_i = c_i • v_i and v_i = c_i • w_i give span(range w) = span(range v).
Linearity of β in slot 0 (map_update_smul with scalar −1, update_eq_self) gives β(w) = −β(v).

subproblem.title: An n-covector pulled back by the orthogonal projection onto a subspace of dimension < n vanishes
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be a linear subspace with dim V < n and orthogonal projection p_V = V.starProjection. Then for every n-covector β on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) the pulled-back covector β∘p_V := β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection, (β∘p_V)(u) = β(p_V u_0, …, p_V u_{n−1}), is the zero covector.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V < n → ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected proof ("For every n-covector β and every u, the n vectors p u_0, …, p u_d lie in V, whose dimension is r < n, so they are linearly dependent, and the alternating map β vanishes on them (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). Thus β∘p = 0"), stated for an arbitrary degree n.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; an n-covector is β : Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ; p := V.starProjection = V.subtypeL ∘L V.orthogonalProjectionOnto, so p x = ↑(V.orthogonalProjectionOnto x) ∈ V (Submodule.starProjection_apply); β∘p := β.compContinuousLinearMap p, with (β∘p)(u) = β(p∘u) = β(p u_0, …, p u_{n−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).
1. (Reduction to values.) Two continuous alternating maps are equal when they agree at every argument family (ext). Fix u : Fin n → ℝ^P; since the zero map takes the value 0 everywhere (ContinuousAlternatingMap.coe_zero), it suffices to prove β(p u_0, …, p u_{n−1}) = 0.
2. (The projected family is linearly dependent.) Suppose the family w := (p u_i)_{i ∈ Fin n} in ℝ^P were linearly independent. Put w'_i := V.orthogonalProjectionOnto u_i ∈ V; then w = V.subtype ∘ w' by the definition of p. If the image of a family under a linear map is linearly independent then so is the family (LinearIndependent.of_comp, applied to the linear map V.subtype); hence w' is a linearly independent family of n vectors in the finite-dimensional space V, and therefore n = card(Fin n) ≤ dim V (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, Fintype.card_fin). This contradicts the hypothesis dim V < n. Hence w is not linearly independent.
3. (Alternating forms vanish on dependent families.) β.toAlternatingMap is an alternating ℝ-multilinear map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ over the field ℝ (a domain, and ℝ is torsion-free over itself); such a map vanishes on every family that is not linearly independent (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). By step 2, β(p∘u) = β.toAlternatingMap(w) = 0.
4. (Conclusion.) As u was arbitrary, β∘p = 0 by step 1. (If n = 0 the hypothesis dim V < 0 is impossible, so the claim is vacuous; the argument above needs no case split.) ∎

theorem Submission.cbr_ci_cp_comp_starProjection_eq_zero_of_finrank_lt : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V < n → ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection = 0 := by
  intro P n V hlt β
  ext u
  rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply]
  apply β.toAlternatingMap.map_linearDependent
  intro hli
  have hli' : LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => V.orthogonalProjectionOnto (u i)) := by
    apply LinearIndependent.of_comp V.subtype
    exact hli
  have hcard := hli'.fintype_card_le_finrank
  rw [Fintype.card_fin] at hcard
  omega
proof_key_steps: Reduce β∘p_V = 0 to β(p_V u_0, …, p_V u_{n−1}) = 0 for every family u (ext, compContinuousLinearMap_apply).
p_V∘u = V.subtype ∘ (orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘ u) is not linearly independent: otherwise LinearIndependent.of_comp gives n linearly independent vectors in V, so n ≤ dim V < n.
An alternating form vanishes on a linearly dependent family (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent), so β(p_V∘u) = 0.

subproblem.title: An n-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P is the span of an orthonormal n-frame
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be a linear subspace with dim V = n. Then there is an orthonormal family v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, indexed by Fin n, with span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} = V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → ∃ v : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the selected proof ("As dim V = n, V has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed along finrank ℝ V = n); let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be its image in ℝ^P. Then v is orthonormal in ℝ^P and span{v_0, …, v_d} = V"), stated for an arbitrary dimension n.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; V carries the restricted inner product and is a finite-dimensional real inner product space; ι := V.subtype : V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ^P is the inclusion, which is the linear isometry V.subtypeₗᵢ.
1. (An orthonormal basis of V indexed by Fin n.) A finite-dimensional real inner product space has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin (finrank): stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V : OrthonormalBasis (Fin (finrank ℝ V)) ℝ V. Reindexing it along the bijection finCongr h : Fin (finrank ℝ V) ≃ Fin n given by the hypothesis h : finrank ℝ V = n (OrthonormalBasis.reindex) yields an orthonormal basis b = (b_0, …, b_{n−1}) of V.
2. (Orthonormal in ℝ^P.) Put v_i := ι(b_i) = ↑b_i ∈ ℝ^P. A linear isometry preserves inner products, so ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = ⟨b_i, b_j⟩ = [i = j]; that is, v is orthonormal in ℝ^P (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry applied to b.orthonormal and V.subtypeₗᵢ).
3. (Span.) range v = ι(range b) (Set.range_comp), so span(range v) = map ι (span(range b)) (Submodule.span_image). The vectors of a basis span the whole space, span(range b) = ⊤ (Basis.span_eq for b.toBasis, whose underlying family is b by OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis). Hence span(range v) = map ι ⊤ = range ι = V (Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).
4. (Conclusion.) v : Fin n → ℝ^P is orthonormal and span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} = V. (For n = 0, V = 0 and v is the empty family; the argument is uniform in n.) ∎

The following proof was compiled in this decomposition session against the frozen import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission (Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c; #print axioms = propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no warnings), both standalone and in situ next to the other children, and it passes the runtime leaf check check_source_delta; it may be used verbatim:
theorem Submission.cbr_ci_cp_exists_orthonormal_frame_of_finrank_eq : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → ∃ v : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V := by
  intro P n V hV
  let b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) ℝ V := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V).reindex (finCongr hV)
  refine ⟨fun i => (b i : Euclid P), ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact b.orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry V.subtypeₗᵢ
  · have hrange : Set.range (fun i => (b i : Euclid P)) = (V.subtype) '' Set.range b := by
      rw [← Set.range_comp]; rfl
    have hb : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range b) = ⊤ := by
      simpa [OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis] using b.toBasis.span_eq
    rw [hrange, Submodule.span_image, hb, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype]
proof_key_steps: Reindex stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V along finrank ℝ V = n to an orthonormal basis b of V indexed by Fin n.
v_i := ↑b_i is orthonormal in ℝ^P because the inclusion V.subtypeₗᵢ is a linear isometry.
span(range v) = map V.subtype (span(range b)) = map V.subtype ⊤ = V.
